taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla occidentalis: stems 1-6 dm. high, silky-villous.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla: scapose perennial herbs with stout rootstocks.

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla: scapose perennial herbs.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: the leaves die back each winter under the snow.

traits.rosette.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla: basal leaves long-petioled.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla: stem leaves 3, forming an involucre remote from the flower: one whorl.

traits.leaves_per_whorl.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla: stem leaves 3, forming an involucre.

traits.leaf_whorls.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla: the 3 stem leaves form one involucre.

traits.leaf_division.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla occidentalis: basal leaves ternate, the divisions twice pinnately dissected.

traits.division_pattern.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla occidentalis: basal leaves ternate: three divisions from the petiole's tip.

traits.division_order.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla occidentalis: the three divisions twice pinnately dissected; drawn divided twice, the finest cuts as dissected segments.

traits.pinnae.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla occidentalis: basal leaves ternate: 3 primary divisions.

traits.inner_division_pattern.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla occidentalis: the divisions pinnately dissected.

traits.leaflets.note: 7 to 11 primary segments along each of the three divisions, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 19238580, 870941, 1623814, 135289630, 113539, 375040248, 59482182, 145592116): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla occidentalis: the ultimate segments narrowly linear and acute: finely dissected.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla occidentalis: the ultimate segments narrowly linear and acute.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: basal blades 4 cm to 10 cm long, as in the photos.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: basal petioles 3 cm to 10 cm long, as in the photos; Abrams (1944 p. 193) calls them long, and the involucral leaves short-petioled.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla occidentalis: the silky-villous divisions.

traits.stem_hairs.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla occidentalis: stems silky-villous.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla: scapose herbs, the involucre remote from the flower: a solitary flower.

traits.perianth.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla: sepals petaloid; petals none: drawn as a single series of tepals.

traits.perianth_parts.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: petaloid sepals 5 to 8, usually 6, as in the photos.

traits.tepal_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla occidentalis: sepals oval to oblong, 20-25 mm. long.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla occidentalis: sepals 20-25 mm. long, cupped, so the flower about 4 cm to 5 cm across, as in the photos.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Sepals held in a shallow cup, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 19238580, 870941, 1623814, 135289630, 113539, 375040248, 59482182, 145592116): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla occidentalis: sepals white or tinged with purple; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.anther_colour.note: Stamens a dense yellow boss; sRGB by eye, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 19238580, 870941, 1623814, 135289630, 113539, 375040248, 59482182, 145592116): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.fruit_type.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla: achenes numerous, forming a head in fruit and furnished with elongated persistent plumose styles.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla occidentalis: achenes villous, the styles long-silky-plumose, 2.5-3 cm. long: each fruit drawn as its achene and plumose style.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: the plumose fruiting heads silvery buff.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 193, Pulsatilla occidentalis: June-Aug.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: the shaggy fruiting heads stand from July to September.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a small clump of finely dissected, silky-hairy leaves, each hairy stem with a whorl of three leaves below one cup-shaped white flower with a yellow boss of stamens. The basal leaves' petiole share is set by hand from the leaf and petiole lengths the traits give, as no rule sets a rosette leaf's.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for western pasqueflower from its sources and the photos the traits cite: the herb program's structure (stems, nodes, basal leaves, how the flowers are borne). The rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.3 m tall at 4 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, 2026-10-19): sizes and forms from Abrams (vols. 2 to 4) and the Range Plant Handbook where it treats the species, counts and colours from iNaturalist photos.
